But what’s more important is that the majority of Orlando’s 3-point shots are coming off kickouts, which, based on data, typically results in more efficient long distance shooting percentages.

The Jazz had three 20-point scorers, with Lauri Markkanen (28), Keyonte George (24), and Jaren Jackson Jr. (20) serving as the team’s leaders.
Utah held Los Angeles to 36-percent shooting from the field in the opening frame, while the home team had a 24-4 advantage in paint scoring after 12 minutes of action.
Ace Bailey set the tone with 15 points and seven rebounds (five on the offensive end) during his first-quarter minutes, while George dished out seven assists in eight minutes.
On the other side, it was a Dončić one-man show, as the Slovenian star put up 17 points.
After a Markkanen 3-pointer at the buzzer, the Jazz held a 47-29 lead after one.

Suffice it to say that if De Larrea shot like that all the time, there’s no way he would have slipped to the No. 25 pick in the draft.
Considering he won’t turn 21 until Dec. 4, De Larrea has oodles of potential and that’s what made him one of the most attractive European players in the draft.
